claims.statement: Harness-owned id allocation stays in the kernel: `next_id` starts at 1, is dense, monotonic and never reused, and persist/snapshot keeps it; packages/entity mirrors the watermark only (`pkg.entity.seq`).

Entities are stored as loose attributes collected under a schema rather than a fixed class hierarchy; every schema field is declared in the package manifest and a field defined out-of-tree is ungoverned.

Invariants I2 (narrow `Value` domain, so no float/int identity split is possible) and I3 (`define`/`set`/`tag` only enter the declared property domain, otherwise `YGG-PKG-ENTITY-ATTR` / `YGG-PKG-ENTITY-SCHEMA`) are the only two gates the package adds; semantics stay in the mod.

The 29-case count is pinned in the in-repo selftest fixture rather than duplicated in prose: `--filter pkg-entity` reports 29 (26 `pkg.entity.*` behaviour cases plus `pkg-entity-paths`' two and the S9 destroy case).

The selftest driver that produces those per-package numbers is `cargo run -q --example selftest -p ygg-sandbox -- --mod packages/mods/pkg-selftest --packages packages/libs [--filter pkg-<name>]`; the full run is 199 cases passed across the eight packages.

The perf figures (`entity.load`, `entity.get_set`, `entity.memory`, `entity.leak`, `entity.paths_*`, `entity.query_face.*`) are asserted by the package's own perf file, so the table cannot drift from the code.

`entity.query`'s selector grammar (`tag` / `where` / `select` / `order` / `schema`) is decoded in the kernel's entity query surface and only wrapped here, which is why the package resolves it in `query.lua`.
